Role Concept: Co-design methods for including people with disability in health communication interventions
Title: Methods for Co-designing Health Communication Initiatives with People with Disability: A Scoping Review
Authors: Kelsey Chapman; Connie Allen; Elizabeth Kendall
Key Frameworks Methods: Scoping review of co-design methods; identifies methods used at different stages and recommends transparency/consistency in reporting co-design processes

Role Concept: Gender-sensitive considerations in assistive technology (AT) design and provision
Title: Outcomes of assistive technology use by sex and gender; a scoping review
Authors: Elizabeth Mc Guinness; Dilisha Patel; Mikaela Patrick; Victoria Austin
Key Frameworks Methods: Scoping review using narrative synthesis informed by the socio-ecological model

Role Concept: System-level challenges and strategies for development/diffusion of assistive technologies (AT) that promote inclusion and well-being
Title: Challenges and strategies for the development and diffusion of assistive technologies
Authors: J. W. Lourenço; Paulo Alexandre Correia de Jesus; Jones Luís Schaefer; Osíris Canciglieri Junior
Key Frameworks Methods: Systematic Literature Review (RSL) as primary methodological approach

Role Concept: Disability-led inclusive design theory foregrounding “disability jugaad” (embodied, improvisational interventions) and participatory approaches
Title: Somaesthetic Socio-Cultural Design for Disability: Rethinking Body Marginality
Authors: Jonathan Ventura; Shilpa Das
Key Frameworks Methods: Disability jugaad; somaesthetics; value-oriented design; emphasizes co-design/participatory design as crucial

Role Concept: Inclusive design for health technologies for users facing limitations (e.g., accessibility for people with disabilities)
Title: Design of health technologies for users facing limitations: A scoping review
Authors: Emanuele König-Klever; Patricia Raquel Bohn; C. Libânio; F. Fogliatto; L. Tonetto
Key Frameworks Methods: Uses accessibility fundamentals recommended by the Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI) as an analytical starting point

Role Concept: Adoption of mobility assistive products; highlights empowerment and incorporating user-centred design considerations in uptake
Title: Understanding adoption of mobility assistive products: a systematic review
Authors: Emily Gleaton; Robert Kistenberg; Lucas E. Provine; Christopher W. Wiese
Key Frameworks Methods: Thematic analysis yielding four overarching themes; advocates more inclusive research design methodologies relevant to assistive products

Role Concept: Shift from assistive toward inclusive technologies to support people with pervasive support needs, assessing effects on quality of life (QoL)
Title: From assistive to inclusive? A systematic review of the uses and effects of technology to support people with pervasive support needs.
Authors: Lotte Piekema; Annet Ten Brug; A. Waninge; A. V. D. van der Putten
Source Journal Book: Journal article (Wiley Online Library PDF link available)
Key Frameworks Methods: PRISMA-based systematic review; uses QoL (sub)domains (Schalock et al.) and ISO 9999:2022 classification for assistive products; discusses technology based on universal design (UD) principles

Role Concept: Integrating systems analysis with user-centred design to engage stakeholders and improve pre-surgical care pathways
Title: INTEGRATING SYSTEMS AND DESIGN THINKING IN HEALTHCARE: A USER-CENTRED PERSPECTIVE
Authors: Christopher Pandolfi; Xavier Massé; Ana Rita Morais; Yefri Ventura; Marko Cigljarev; Angela Jerath
Key Frameworks Methods: Systems analysis + user-centred design tools including ecosystem mapping, participatory workshops, journey mapping, and data visualization artifacts (interactive journey maps, matrices, rose charts)

Role Concept: Usability and ergonomic design as determinants of user acceptance and preference in medical devices/equipment
Title: Medical Device and Equipment Design
Authors: Michael E. Wiklund
Source Journal Book: Book: Medical Device and Equipment Design
Key Frameworks Methods: Ergonomic design principles and usability-oriented guidance for medical device and equipment design

Role Concept: User-centred design (UCD) for sustainable health technology: involving end-users throughout development to ensure usability and value
Title: User centered design for the development of health technology: Towards sustainable healthcare systems
Authors: Sara S Groos
Key Frameworks Methods: Interdisciplinary overview of UCD methods (communication science, health psychology, marketing, health informatics); methods include personas, think-aloud, prototypes, focus groups; identifies stages where participation is crucial and barriers to participation

Role Concept: Systematic review of how autistic people are involved in design of XR technologies, with roles ranging from contributors to co-designers; proposes an inclusion framework
Title: How are Autistic People Involved in the Design of Extended Reality Technologies? A Systematic Literature Review
Authors: Nigel Newbutt; Noah J. Glaser; Marc-Sonley Francois; Matthew Schmidt; S. Cobb
Key Frameworks Methods: PRISMA; PICo framework; proposes a design framework characterizing autistic inclusion in XR research; defines co-design as users being active participants and equal contributors

Role Concept: Evaluating effectiveness of universal design (UD) outcomes in healthcare and other sectors by measuring performance and participation/inclusion
Title: Developing Innovative Solutions for Universal Design in Healthcare and Other Sectors
Authors: Jonathan White; E. I. Mosca
Key Frameworks Methods: Reviews evaluations of UD tools including Design for All A.U.D.I.T. and isUD; describes a hierarchical UD quality framework (physical-spatial; sensorial-cognitive; social) derived from systematic review, workshops with users/experts, and hospital-setting analyses

Role Concept: Systematic review on how inaccessible urban public spaces affect mobility assistive device users; proposes human-centred approaches and discusses universal design benefits
Title: Disabled-by-design: effects of inaccessible urban public spaces on users of mobility assistive devices
Authors: Efthimis Kapsalis; Nils Jaeger; Jonathan Hale
Key Frameworks Methods: PRISMA; Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT); systematic search terms organized around review axes (MobAD, quality of life, physical elements)

Role Concept: Participatory co-design (PCD) as a strategy to strengthen implementation, scale-up, spread, and sustainability of assistive technology with older adults
Title: Supporting Healthy Aging through the Scale-Up, Spread, and Sustainability of Assistive Technology Implementation: A Rapid Realist Review of Participatory Co-Design for Assistive Technology with Older Adults
Authors: S. Carroll; K. Kobayashi; Matilde N. Cervantes; Shannon Freeman; Manik Saini; Shannon Tracey
Key Frameworks Methods: NASSS (Non-Adoption, Scale-up, Spread, and Sustainability) framework; rapid realist review steps aligned with Saul et al. (2013) and Pawson et al. (2005); develops program theories of context–mechanism–outcome interactions

Role Concept: Participatory design (PD) techniques and challenges for technology design with autistic people and people with cognitive disabilities; emphasizes empowerment via participation
Title: Participatory Technology Design for Autism and Cognitive Disabilities: A Narrative Overview of Issues and Techniques
Authors: Nigel Robb; Bryan Boyle; Yurgos Politis; N. Newbutt; H. Kuo; Connie Sung
Key Frameworks Methods: Defines PD as user involvement in design/development; overview of PD techniques and challenges for novice PD researchers/designers

Role Concept: Universal Design as an industrial design paradigm for health interventions for older adults; positions ID professionals as part of caregiving team
Title: Universal Design as a Paradigm for Providing Health Interventions for Older Adults 1
Authors: Peter J. Snyder
Key Frameworks Methods: Frames Universal Design as an industrial design (ID) approach with inclusivity as hallmark characteristic

Role Concept: Critical reframing of (dis)ability in design using critical disability studies and universal/inclusive design perspectives
Title: Refactoring design to reframe (dis)ability
Authors: E. Churchill
Key Frameworks Methods: Critical Disability Studies (CDS) with discussion of universal design and inclusive design; frames UD as expanding usability to all people

Role Concept: Universal Design and ergonomics to identify inclusive requirements for assistive orthopedic products (rheumatoid arthritis hand disabilities)
Title: Comparison of Assistive Orthopedic Products using the Pugh Matrix. A Universal Design and Ergonomics Approach
Authors: A. López; Juan Luis Hernández Arellano; Edson Francisco Estrada Meneses
Source Journal Book: Cultura Científica y Tecnológica, Vol. 18, Issue 1 (January–April 2021)
Key Frameworks Methods: Pugh matrix for comparing/evaluating products; uses Universal Design and ergonomics; includes QOL-RA scale and Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ)

Role Concept: Inclusive design and interdisciplinary links (including healthcare and medical device design) emphasized in Inclusive Design Research and CWUAAT proceedings
Title: DESIGNING INCLUSIVE SYSTEMS
Authors: Michal Skrzypczak; P. Hofman
Source Journal Book: Proceedings volume from The Cambridge Workshops on Universal Access and Assistive Technology (CWUAAT)
Key Frameworks Methods: Inclusive Design Research described as developing tools and guidance to design for the widest possible population; notes interdisciplinary links with healthcare and medical device design

Role Concept: Human-centred design (HCD) for medical devices/diagnostics in global health; aims for usability, durability, and affordability in low-resource environments
Title: Human-centered design for medical devices and diagnostics in global health
Authors: Mark Fisher; E. Johansen
Key Frameworks Methods: Overviews HCD processes/methods/mindsets; HCD draws on ethnography, participatory design/co-design, contextual design, empathic design; uses journey maps, stakeholder maps, personas; references ISO/IEC 62366 for formative/summative human factors testing

Role Concept: Barriers to assistive technology use; argues for moving away from traditional medical model toward greater user involvement for personalised care
Title: Exploring the barriers to using assistive technology for individuals with chronic conditions: a meta-synthesis review
Authors: J. Howard; Z. Fisher; A. Kemp; Stephen Lindsay; L. Tasker; J. Tree
Key Frameworks Methods: Meta-synthesis using GENIAL framework, ICF, PRISMA, CASP checklist, and ARCHIE framework

Role Concept: Highlights mismatch between textbook user-centred design and healthcare-sector practice; critiques technology-driven medical product design processes
Title: THE HEALTHCARE DESIGN DILEMMA: PERILS OF A TECHNOLOGY-DRIVEN DESIGN PROCESS FOR MEDICAL PRODUCTS
Authors: H. Wilke; P. Badke-Schaub; K. Thoring
Key Frameworks Methods: Case study approach (Yin, 2009) using participatory observation, diary studies, semi-structured interviews, and document/job-posting analysis; references experience-based co-design (EBCD)

Role Concept: Design translation challenges in healthcare: argues that alongside UCD/co-design, early engagement of broader stakeholders is needed for adoption/implementation
Title: Design in healthcare: the challenge of translation
Authors: J. West
Source Journal Book: Royal College of Art (RCA) Research Online repository PDF
Key Frameworks Methods: Case studies leading to proposed methodology to optimize inclusive design in healthcare; uses Design Council Double Diamond as core process model and references Inclusive Design toolkit (Engineering Design Centre)

Role Concept: Participatory design as a route to accessible technology; emphasizes collaboration/communication among actors in design processes
Title: A review: accessible technology through participatory design
Authors: Christian Quintero
Key Frameworks Methods: Expert-developed protocol of guidelines; assesses literature across accessibility, assistive technologies, and participatory design categories

Role Concept: Performance-based Universal Design assessment tool supporting designers and healthcare management to promote inclusion in healthcare environments
Title: Universal Design assessment tool to promote well-being and inclusion in healthcare environment
Authors: E. I. Mosca; E. Steinfeld; S. Capolongo
Source Journal Book: European Journal of Public Health (supplement PDF available)
Key Frameworks Methods: Systematic literature review of UD tools; workshops with users/experts; analysis of hospital case studies; multi-criteria analysis to develop hierarchical framework; checklist-based rating system with categories/criteria/indicators

Role Concept: User involvement in assistive technology service delivery processes (AT-SDP) to achieve positive outcomes
Title: The effects of assistive technology service delivery processes and factors associated with positive outcomes
Authors: Not mentioned in source.
Key Frameworks Methods: European AT-SDP generic model steps (initiative → assessment → typology → selection → financing → delivery → follow-up); uses Joanna Briggs Institute MAStARI critical appraisal tools; PRISMA reporting guideline

Role Concept: Human factors for designing home-based stroke rehabilitation technologies: engagement/motivation and designing for home context
Title: Home-based technologies for stroke rehabilitation: A systematic review
Authors: Yu Chen; Kingsley Travis Abel; John T. Janecek; Yunan Chen; Kai Zheng; S. Cramer
Key Frameworks Methods: Derives two main human factors: designing for engagement (external/internal motivation) and designing for the home environment (social context, practical challenges, technical proficiency)

Role Concept: Therapists’ experiences highlight the need for collaboration with technology developers to improve design/usability of rehabilitation technologies
Title: Experiences of therapists using feedback-based technology to improve physical function in rehabilitation settings: a qualitative systematic review
Authors: Caitlin Hamilton; Meryl Lovarini; A. McCluskey; Tarcisio Folly de Campos; Leanne Hassett
Key Frameworks Methods: Thematic synthesis of qualitative studies; NVivo-assisted coding and categorisation

Role Concept: Patient-centred (user-centred) design case study in connected healthcare contexts
Title: Patient-Centered Design in a Connected Healthcare World: A Case Study
Authors: N. Dey; P. Rautray; M. Soni
Key Frameworks Methods: Not mentioned in source.

Role Concept: Industrial design in medical devices: emphasizes multidisciplinary collaboration (biomedical engineering + industrial design) and user needs
Title: The Importance of Industrial Design in Medical Devices in the 21st Century
Authors: Fanny Guadalupe Valdivia-Márquez; Pilar Hernandez-Grageda; Gabriela Durán-Aguilar; Luis Alberto Rosa Sierra
Key Frameworks Methods: Highlights multidisciplinary work among biomedical engineering and industrial design with support from ergonomics and psychology to meet user needs

Role Concept: Medical device design challenges: argues for considering a “hierarchy of users” and prioritizing needs by illness stage; notes absence of industrial designers in device design
Title: Medical Device Design Challenges Based on Users Hierarchy and Their Correlation with Illness
Authors: Fabiola Cortes-Chavez; Maria Giovanna-Trotta; Paulina Manzano-Hernandez; Luis Alberto Rosa Sierra; Gabriela Durán-Aguilar
Key Frameworks Methods: Human-centred design methodologies; concept of “hierarchy of users” to prioritize user needs by illness stage

Role Concept: Human-centred criteria for healthcare design to integrate human factors and reduce misuse across the design process
Title: Human centred criteria for healthcare design
Authors: A. Millet; A. A. Akle; J. Legardeur
Key Frameworks Methods: Presents stage-specific criteria; notes directives/standards requiring integration of human factors to reduce risks of misuse and guide design

Role Concept: Design for care and therapeutic wellbeing: develops a “Design for Care” model using qualitative data to improve medical products
Title: Designing Care. How Design can improve medical products for a therapeutic wellbeing
Authors: Angela Giambattista
Key Frameworks Methods: Evidence-Based Design (EBD), User-Centred Design, Research Through Design; introduces the “Care Scale” and translates observations into a “Design for Care” model

Role Concept: Assistive technology in daily life: overview of knowledge in rehabilitation and calls for integrative models supporting collaboration among actors across the technological continuum
Title: Use of assistive technologies in daily life: A portrait of current knowledge
Authors: Pierre-Yves Therriault; Marie-Michèle Lord; Alexe Desaulnier; Galaad Lefay
Key Frameworks Methods: Interpretative synthesis methodology based on Pope et al. (2007)

Role Concept: Systematic review of users’ needs for assistive technology for upper extremities after stroke; links attention to user perspectives to improved fit and acceptance
Title: Assistive Technology for the Upper Extremities After Stroke: Systematic Review of Users’ Needs
Authors: A. L. van Ommeren; L. C. Smulders; Gerdienke B. Prange-Lasonder; J. Buurke; P. Veltink; J. Rietman
Key Frameworks Methods: Synthesizes qualitative user-perspective data; included studies used focus groups, questionnaires, and interviews; explicitly links user-centred design attention to better-fitting devices

Role Concept: Assistive technology provision for children: systematic review of factors influencing provision and selection; highlights consumer-/family-centered decision-making frameworks
Title: Factors Perceived by Rehabilitation Professionals to Influence the Provision of Assistive Technology to Children: A Systematic Review
Authors: Karin van Niekerk; S. Dada; K. Tönsing; K. Boshoff
Key Frameworks Methods: Uses Assistive Technology Device Selection Framework (Scherer et al., 2007); references HAAT model and Matching Person and Technology model; deductive then inductive thematic analysis; MMAT used for quality appraisal

Role Concept: Co-creation of personal medical devices (PMDs) and orthotics: patient involvement as co-designers to improve wellbeing and adherence
Title: Quantified Lives and Vital Data
Authors: R. Lynch; C. Farrington
Key Frameworks Methods: Case study of orthotics with patients as co-designers; considers solutions within a biopsychosocial model of healthcare

Role Concept: User-centred ergonomics in NICU medical device design: iterative development shaped by key users (nursing staff)
Title: The Role of Ergonomics in the Design of an Intravenous Therapy (IV) Set for Neonatal Intensive Care
Authors: A. Albayrak; M.M.A. Vreede; L. Evers; R. Goossens
Key Frameworks Methods: Contextual design methods including observations and interviews with stakeholders (especially nursing staff), generative sessions, and multiple user feedback sessions; multiple design iterations based on user needs/limitations in context

Role Concept: Systematic review of inclusive toys for rehabilitation: discusses co-design/adapting accessible interactive toys supported by participatory design techniques
Title: Inclusive Toys for Rehabilitation of Children with Disability: A Systematic Review
Authors: Eunice P. dos Santos Nunes; Vicente António da Conceição Júnior; Lucas Vinicius Giraldelli Santos; Maurício Fernando L. Pereira; L. C. L. F. Borges
Key Frameworks Methods: Co-design and/or adapting accessible toys; PD techniques; proposes a conception/design model for inclusive toys supported by PD techniques

Role Concept: Foundational discussion of user-centred and participatory design approaches in assistive technology development
Title: The Design and Development of Assistive Technology
Authors: N. Harris
Key Frameworks Methods: Discusses user-centered design (UCD) and participatory design (PD) as key approaches

Role Concept: Paradigm shift in assistive technology design from user-centred design to co-creation, with users central and directly connected to designers
Title: Disrupting the world of Disability: The Next Generation of Assistive Technologies and Rehabilitation Practices.
Authors: C. Holloway; H. Dawes
Source Journal Book: Healthcare Technology Letters (Wiley PDF link available)
Key Frameworks Methods: Highlights user-centred design methods and a shift toward co-creation; also discusses positive design and positive computing as relevant lenses

Role Concept: User participation in medical device development processes and the role of industrial design; argues users are often passive participants in regulated development and suggests richer user involvement practices
Title: COLLABORATIVE DESIGN PROCESSES IN MEDICAL DEVICE DEVELOPMENT
Authors: M. Privitera; D. Southee
Key Frameworks Methods: Literature review of device development processes; suggests contextual inquiry and formal usability assessments; highlights transfer of user-involvement practices from consumer product design to medical devices

Role Concept: User involvement techniques in assistive technology new product development (AT NPD), emphasizing user-centred collaboration across phases
Title: An evaluation of the potential order and priority of research methods, design methods and design heuristics within an Assistive Technology new product development process
Authors: G. Torrens
Key Frameworks Methods: Defines 61 research/design methods and heuristics; relates method clustering to Martin & Hanington’s 5-phase design process model (phase emphasis noted)

Role Concept: Universal design applied as a patient-centred approach to improve healthcare services and patient experience
Title: Make It Better: how universal design principles can have an impact on healthcare services to improve the patient experience
Authors: J. Myerson; J. West
Key Frameworks Methods: Examines the Seven Principles of Universal Design (Ron Mace, 1997) and evaluates which are relevant to healthcare; uses case studies from The Helen Hamlyn Centre for Design (RCA)

Role Concept: Industrial design as addressing physical and emotional human needs; promotes human-centred and empathic research strategies in healthcare-related product design projects
Title: Innovating alongside designers.
Authors: D. McDonagh; Joyce Thomas
Key Frameworks Methods: Human-centred/empathic research strategies (ethnography, empathic modelling, shared language, collaboration); iterative toolkit methods including user research, prototyping, and usability testing

Role Concept: Evidence-based, user-centric integration of medical, assistive, and universal-design technologies via service methods and classification frameworks
Title: Integrating medical, assistive, and universal design products and technologies: Assistive Technology Service Method (ATSM)
Authors: Linda-Jeanne Elsaesser; S. Bauer
Source Journal Book: Disability & Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology (referenced as source of related articles)
Key Frameworks Methods: Assistive Technology Service Method (ATSM), Assistive Technology Device Classification (ATDC), Matching Person and Technology (MPT); uses ICF conceptual framework/common language

Role Concept: ICF-based classification differentiating medical, assistive, and universally designed products; supports universal design principles and informs rehabilitation practice/public policy
Title: Integrating medical, assistive, and universally designed products and technologies: assistive technology device classification (ATDC)
Authors: S. Bauer; Linda-Jeanne Elsaesser
Key Frameworks Methods: ATDC, ATSM, and Matching Person and Technology models as a standardized, internationally comparable framework; grounded in ICF language and concepts

Role Concept: Inclusive design as a business/industry imperative; aims to minimise preventable design exclusion using data-driven methods to understand user diversity
Title: Designing a More Inclusive World
Authors: S. Keates; J. Clarkson; P. Langdon; P. Robinson
Source Journal Book: Edited book inspired by Cambridge Workshops on Universal Access and Assistive Technology (CWUAAT)
Key Frameworks Methods: Representative user methods (market segmentation, personas, impairment simulation); predictive population datasets for task exclusion; exclusion audit procedures and tools validated against survey data

Role Concept: User involvement in early assistive technology (AT) development; evaluates methods to elicit needs and test early designs
Title: User involvement in the early development of assistive technology devices
Authors: Z. Clarke; S. Judge; N. Heron; Joe Langley; I. Hosking; M. Hawley
Key Frameworks Methods: Four user involvement methods: focus groups, online surveys, qualitative interviews, and design workshops; includes an inclusive design approach and a needs–solutions–evaluation toolkit (three fundamental questions)

Role Concept: Conceptual framework for integrating users into medical device development (MDD) via cross-disciplinary user requirements research
Title: THE ROLE OF USER REQUIREMENTS RESEARCH IN MEDICAL DEVICE DEVELOPMENT
Authors: Anila Shah; S. Alshawi
Key Frameworks Methods: Constructs a conceptual framework for user involvement in MDD by amalgamating methods from IT, ergonomics (including participatory research), psychology, and design

Role Concept: Inclusive design reframes disability as a mismatch created by designs/environments; summarizes active inclusive design research topics and methods
Title: Inclusive design
Authors: John Clarkson; Roger Coleman
Source Journal Book: Taylor & Francis journal publication (ISSNs and DOI provided)
Key Frameworks Methods: Discusses inclusive design management (BS 7000-6), researcher–user engagement, and user research methods as part of inclusive design tooling and education efforts
